item.title: Personal finance
item.description: Language for budgeting, borrowing, saving and investing your own money.

children.definition: a record of how reliably a person has borrowed and paid back money
children.example: Newcomers abroad often struggle to rent a flat because they have no credit history there.

children.definition: the money left after paying tax and essential bills
children.example: Once the loan is paid off, our disposable income will rise noticeably.

children.definition: one of several regular payments that together pay for something
children.example: She is paying for the laptop in twelve monthly instalments.

children.definition: an arrangement that lets you take more money from your bank account than you have in it
children.example: Using an overdraft every month can become very expensive.

children.definition: property you promise to a lender, which they can take if you do not repay
children.example: The bank asked him to use his car as collateral.

children.definition: owing money because you have spent more than you have
children.example: My account was in the red by the end of the holiday.

children.definition: money kept aside for unexpected costs such as losing a job or a medical bill
children.example: Financial advisers often suggest an emergency fund that covers several months of expenses.

children.definition: to spread your money across different types of investment to reduce risk
children.example: Rather than buying shares in one company, she diversified across several funds.

children.definition: a general rise in prices that makes money worth less over time
children.example: If your savings earn less than inflation, they are effectively shrinking.

children.definition: money that someone working abroad sends home to their family
children.example: He sends a remittance to his parents in Andijan every month.

children.definition: something you buy suddenly without planning or thinking carefully
children.example: The smartwatch was an impulse buy that I hardly use.

children.definition: to have just enough money to pay for the things you need
children.example: As a student abroad, she took a part-time job to make ends meet.
